subtitles.en: Man, I have that huge live presentation this afternoon.
subtitles.zh: 天啊，我今天下午有一場超大的現場簡報。

subtitles.en: You are gonna do great. Break a leg.
subtitles.zh: 你一定會表現超棒的，祝你順利，Break a leg！

subtitles.en: Wait, break my leg? Why would you curse me like that?
subtitles.zh: 等等，打斷我的腿？妳幹嘛這樣詛咒我啊？

subtitles.en: I am not cursing you, Alex. Relax.
subtitles.zh: 我才沒有詛咒你勒，Alex，放輕鬆啦！

subtitles.en: Then why did you literally tell me to snap my bone?
subtitles.zh: 那妳幹嘛照字面叫我把骨頭折斷？

subtitles.en: Classic mistake. Never translate idioms word for word.
subtitles.zh: 經典錯誤！成語千萬不能逐字硬翻啦。

subtitles.en: Break a leg means good luck. It's an old theater superstition.
subtitles.zh: Break a leg 是祝你好運，這是劇場界的老迷信。

subtitles.en: So bad words bring good fortune.
subtitles.zh: 所以講觸霉頭的話，反而能帶來好運？

subtitles.en: So if someone is super nervous before going on stage, you say?
subtitles.zh: 所以如果有人上台前超緊張，你就可以說…？
